recommendedTitle: Public api+ multipart routes buffer the whole request body with no byte cap
summary: POST /api/contact-form is a public, unauthenticated multipart route: the route module re-exports the action (app/routes/api+/contact-form.tsx:1), the path is in scripts/baselines/route-tree.txt:68, and the repository's own API surface…
currentBehavior: POST /api/contact-form is a public, unauthenticated multipart route: the route module re-exports the action (app/routes/api+/contact-form.tsx:1), the path is in scripts/baselines/route-tree.txt:68, and the repository's own API surface inventory lists it as publicUnauthenticated (docs/api-surface-inventory.md:64). The action reads the body with await request.formData() at app/routes/api+/contact-form.action.server.ts:36 - no byte cap - before any of its own field limits run. An anonymous multipart POST carrying a 32 MiB body made the shared web process grow by 64.5 MiB of resident memory inside the request (measured: 202.4 MiB -> 270.1 MiB peak RSS, still 269.5 MiB after a forced GC), and…
rootCause: The request-body size check this codebase already implements as app/lib/bounded-form-data.server.ts#readBoundedFormData was applied only to the media upload surfaces. Every other multipart route under app/routes/api+ calls the platform's request.formData() directly, which reads the entire body into process memory before any field validation runs, so the bytes one caller can make the shared web process hold are bounded only by the transport's own per-request default (Bun's 128 MB, node_modules/bun-types/serve.d.ts:676, not overridden at server/bun.ts:357) and by nothing at all in aggregate.
resolution: Read every request body through the reader this codebase already has. Replace each direct request.formData() in app/routes/api+ with readBoundedFormData(request, cap) and map FormBodyError to its 413 status, choosing a cap from the route's own field limits (a few tens of KiB for the contact form, a few hundred KiB for survey submissions). Apply the same to the authenticated variants (audiodrop, surveys). As defence in depth, set an explicit maxRequestBodySize on Bun.serve so the transport, not just the handler, bounds a request body; keep it above the largest legitimate body (the media upload cap is 10 MiB + 64 KiB).
existingTests: Bun 1.3.14 in the sandbox (the production Docker image pins oven/bun:1.3.5 and package.json allows bun >=1.2.15). request.formData() over a streamed 32 MiB multipart body: +67.8 MB resident (2.02x body). Real POST /api/contact-form action, 32 MiB body with the honeypot filled: peak RSS 202.4 -> 270.1 MiB (+64.5 MiB,…
missingTests: A regression test for this behaviour fails on the current source and passes with the fix (kill-check: revert the fix and confirm the test goes red).
A negative control for the same path keeps passing, so the fix does not silently widen access.
acceptanceCriteria: A route should read a request body only through a reader that caps the bytes it will consume and rejects an oversized body with 413, so that a field-level limit (MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH, MAX_NAME_LENGTH, a honeypot) bounds the work rather than being validated after the fact. readBoundedFormData(request, maxBytes) already does exactly this and is used by the media surfaces for a ~10 MiB body, with the repository's own test suite (test/bounded-form-data.test.ts) asserting the 413 and the early stream cancellation. The public and authenticated multipart routes should use the same reader with a cap sized for their own fields, and the transport should carry an explicit maxRequestBodySize as a backstop.

summary: CallCaster produces machine-dialed IVR campaign calls from two paths, and they enforce different consent rules
currentBehavior: CallCaster produces machine-dialed IVR campaign calls from two paths, and they enforce different consent rules. The durable worker path (app/lib/campaign-ivr-dispatch.server.ts) reads the recipient's consent state and the campaign's calling window before it dials: it defers a row outside the recipient-local 8am-9pm window (:252), dequeues a member whose contact has opt_out = true instead of dialling (:264), and re-checks the campaign calling policy at the provider boundary (:303, :373). The session-authenticated HTTP route (app/routes/api+/ivr.action.server.ts) reimplements the per-contact mechanics and enforces neither gate: to_number, contact_id, queue_id and campaign_id are taken…
rootCause: The HTTP route re-implements the per-contact send mechanics instead of sharing the dispatcher's eligibility gate, so the consent and window checks that live in the worker dispatcher (app/lib/campaign-ivr-dispatch.server.ts:252, :264, :303) and in the queue-claim and get_campaign_queue RPCs are absent from the send path. The route trusts the request body for the recipient, contact and queue identifiers, never reads contact.opt_out, never resolves the campaign for its calling window, and places the provider call before the queue row is touched, so no state can veto the dial.

recommendedTitle: Tenant-facing GET /api/numbers falls back to the platform parent-account Twilio credential when workspace_id is omitted
summary: Workspace-only number search is implemented in PR #3078. Full local CI, focused tests and three mutation checks pass; review, merge and release verification remain.
currentBehavior: PR #3078 rejects missing or blank workspace_id with 400, checks membership before creating a client, preserves uniform non-member 404 and searches only through createWorkspaceTwilioInstance. The dev branch still has the parent-account fallback.
rootCause: The optional workspace_id selected the provider identity. Omitting it bypassed membership and constructed a parent-account client. A broad provider catch also changed membership 404 into 500.
resolution: Require workspace_id, remove the parent fallback, and await membership outside the provider error handler. Keep local and toll-free searches on the workspace client. Mark workspace_id required in both published OpenAPI documents.

Restoring the old loader fails four tests; removing membership fails four; making the contract optional fails two. Three authentication/validation controls pass in every mutation run. recommendedTitle: Rate-limit failed password checks when disabling 2FA in account security
summary: An authenticated ordinary account can repeat failed password checks on the local 2FA disable path without an application limiter.
currentBehavior: An isolated current-source probe made 15 wrong-password requests using the real local limiter module; all 15 reached the mocked disable API and returned Invalid password. The route checks session freshness and refuses protected accounts; no factor was removed.
rootCause: The enable and TOTP verification branches have user-scoped setup limiters. The disable branch calls Better Auth disableTwoFactor without one.
resolution: Add a user-scoped limiter before the disable password check and include that credential surface in the guard. Preserve protected-account refusal and successful ordinary-account disable behavior.
existingTests: Private scratch probe: 15 requests reached a mocked password provider. The working source hash stayed unchanged. This proves admission behavior, not password bypass or factor removal.
missingTests: Exhaustion blocks before the password provider; separate users and reset windows retain their own budgets.
Protected accounts remain refused, and an ordinary correct-password disable still works.
The regression must fail when its limiter is removed.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed disable password checks are limited by the authenticated user identity before the provider call.
The source coverage guard detects a missing or wrong limiter on this operation.
